summary: Depth at fixed width 512 was the big win: the ladder at the original 2**19 batch ran 8=1.012347, 10=1.003924, 12=1.001467, and depth 12 composed superadditively with a0's TOTAL_BATCH_SIZE 2**18 to give 0.986500 (parts were -0.011 and -0.0087, composition -0.0258 vs baseline). Adding a2's short window 512 on top, keeping DEVICE_BATCH_SIZE 128, gave my best and the cell best, 0.984417 at 65.1GB. What did not work: widening (MODEL_DIM 640 at depth 12 = 0.990459), depth 14 = 0.993330, and every stack that had to drop to device batch 64 / accum 2 to fit VRAM landed 0.988-0.996 even though grad accumulation is mathematically identical, so micro-batch size costs several thousandths on its own. Capacity knobs that helped at depth 8 (per-channel lambdas, MLP_RATIO 6) largely stopped helping at depth 12; the short window is the exception because it buys steps instead of spending them. Next I would test MLP_RATIO 6 at depth 12 with whatever memory saving keeps device batch at 128, and combine with a3's longer WARMDOWN_RATIO 0.7 (0.985510 standalone on my base).
